atoms.text: Marmite is based on yeast extract, invented by German scientist Justus von Liebig during the late 19th century. Marmite is known for its distinctive, strong, salty flavour. The essence of its taste is represented by the famous slogan: “love it or hate it”. The first Marmite factory was built in 1902, but what really kicked off Marmite’s fame as the nation’s favourite snack was learning that Marmite was chock-full of B-vitamins. British troops were given Marmite as part of their rations during World War I to combat the vitamin deficiencies that were common among soldiers. Marmite is best enjoyed spread thin on toast, bread, or crackers with a bit of butter, and is often paired with cheese.
